scope: The RTX 3090 joins as a native Windows lane. RTX 3090 native Windows runs v0.6.2-qwen38-3090-beta.1 (package da1d62f2, server 11b3f93c, source f08309da): the RTX 5090 v0.6.14 source e20060b6 plus one controller fix, built for sm_86, with serving configuration 0f700667, 131,072 tokens of INT8 KV, an 8192 MiB host-KV pool and one request at a time. RTX 5090 stays on v0.6.14-qwen38-5090-beta.1 (image 4c816b0c, server f62a570e, source e20060b6) with profile qwen38-5090-v0.9.0 (configuration cf1de114) and two requests in flight, and RTX 4090 native Windows stays on v0.6.10-qwen38-4090-beta.1 (package a0ea4c81, server e0498fad, source cba7eb93) with configuration 7a69481f and one request at a time. The model artifact, the RTX 5090 and RTX 4090 memory floors and the unmodified upstream OMP 18.4.0 client are unchanged; the RTX 3090 serves the same model artifact and declares no host-memory floor. The RTX 3090 gates are the canonical qualification of the published package on the physical RTX 3090; the RTX 5090 and RTX 4090 gates are carried from v0.9.0.

Publication workflow 36635266542 binds binary archive 386f6849 to image 4c816b0c. The image pull by digest with an empty Docker config verified ninfer-serve f62a570e inside, and every lane-window arm checks that its declared binary identity is the image's.

stock_client_sessions.method: scripts/stock_omp_session_proof.py: the unmodified upstream Oh My Pi 18.4.0 macOS arm64 binary in RPC mode with PI_OPENAI_STATEFUL=1, using the documented macOS route's provider fragment and this release's fail-closed config verbatim (examples/manual-tunnel/models.fragment.yml and fail-closed.yml: async compaction on, two requests in flight per RTX 5090 provider) over an SSH forward on the route's tunnel port 18089. s1: one OMP process seeds two facts, recalls one, the server restarts, and it recalls both; s2: a new OMP process continues the session with the server up; s3: the server restarts, then a new OMP process continues it. Each restart is a graceful stop and a start on the same checkpoint root.

rtx3090_windows_native.rollback_note: Both directions were exercised between candidate qwen38-3090-native-v0.6.2-beta.1-f08309da3cc1 and predecessor qwen38-3090-native-v0.6.0-beta.1-03f56e58ec1b, the lane's only earlier native package, which was never published: its own 2026-09-09 window failed the agent protocol phase. The candidate declares stop-event and stopped gracefully without forced termination. The predecessor predates the stop-event channel and declares terminate; its stop was a forced termination, as that mode provides. The candidate was active again afterwards. The first window, at e20060b6, failed this phase: its controller could not launch a predecessor whose packaged configuration predates context_cache.host_kv_mib, which f08309da fixes.

interpretation: The RTX 3090 joins as a native Windows lane; nothing changes for the RTX 5090 and RTX 4090 lanes. On the physical RTX 3090 the package published as v0.6.2-qwen38-3090-beta.1 passed all 15 lifecycle phases: 130,048-token retrieval exactly in 221.0 s, restart with a managed-stop flush of an unpublished session, rollback in both directions against the lane's unpublished v0.6.0-beta.1 package, protected state with two low-privilege read denials, the 15-check agent protocol at the shipped host pool and with 8 host-state slots, the unmodified upstream OMP 18.4.0 client's typed tool call, and the C1 benchmark at 102.64 tokens/s with 93.43% MTP acceptance under the lane's 300 W cap. The first window, at e20060b6, failed its rollback phase: the shared controller read context_cache.host_kv_mib directly under PowerShell strict mode, and v0.6.0's packaged configuration predates that field, so the managed wrapper exited before launching the predecessor. f08309da reads the field only when a release's configuration declares it, as it already read gpu_keep_warm_ms, and a lifecycle-tree test now requires every configuration field newer than the shipped lineage to be read that way; every published RTX 4090 package declares the field. A managed start refuses while any process holds 1 GiB or more of GPU memory: on the qualification host a signed-in desktop's compositor held about 1,070 MiB, so the window ran with the console signed out. Automatic checkpoints stay best effort and universal warm reuse is not claimed.
